problems.title: Two Sum
problems.problem_summary: Given an integer array and a target, return the indices of two different numbers whose sum equals the target.

hints.text: Before choosing a method, ask yourself: for the current number, which value would complete the target?
If you have already seen the needed value, you only need a fast way to find where you saw it. What information could you store as you scan?
Try maintaining a lookup from each number to its index. For every new number, check whether target minus that number is already in the lookup.
For each index and value: compute complement = target - value. If complement exists in the lookup, return its stored index and the current index. Otherwise store value with its index.
This scans the array once and uses a hash map for fast lookups, so time complexity is O(n). Check the complement before storing the current number so one element is not used twice.

problems.title: Recursive Factorial
problems.problem_summary: Return the factorial of a non-negative integer using recursion.

hints.text: What is the smallest input for which factorial has an answer without another recursive call?
Each call should make the input smaller. Which single arithmetic operation links n to the factorial of a smaller number?
Define a base case for zero or one. Otherwise, combine the current number with the result of solving factorial for one less.
If n is zero or one, return one. Otherwise return n multiplied by factorial of n minus one.
The base case stops recursion, while the recursive case reduces n each time. This takes O(n) time and O(n) call-stack space.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.problem_summary: Choose two vertical lines that form a container holding the maximum possible water.

hints.text: The area depends on both the distance between lines and the shorter height. Which of these can increase when two pointers move inward?
Start at the two ends. If one height is shorter, moving the taller line cannot make the current limiting height larger. Which pointer is worth moving?
Keep left and right pointers. Compute the area, remember the best one, then move the pointer at the shorter line inward.
While left is before right: calculate width times the smaller height, update the maximum, then move left if its height is smaller; otherwise move right.
Moving the shorter boundary is the only chance to improve the limiting height. Each pointer moves at most once across the array, giving O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
